blocks.prompt: 7. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\).
blocks.explanation:
Right side mein sirf \(x\) hai, \(y\) bilkul nahi (yani \(h(y) = 1\)). Is liye equation separable hai aur \(y = \int f(x)\,dx\).
Mushkil sirf integral mein hai: fraction ke neeche ek linear factor \((1 - x)\) aur ek quadratic factor \((1 + x^2)\) hai.
Rule kaunsa? Partial fractions (fraction ko chhote aasaan fractions mein torna).
Plan: partial fractions banayenge, har hissa alag integrate karenge, aur logs ko jor kar ek jawab banayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\).
Maloom karna: general solution.
Tareeqa: \(h(y) = 1\) wali separable equation hai, to \(dy = f(x)\,dx\) likh kar seedha integrate karenge. \(f(x)\) ko integrate karne ke liye pehle partial fractions mein torenge.

Alag karein
\[dy = \dfrac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\,dx\]
Kyun: Dono taraf \(dx\) se multiply kiya. \(y\) to pehle hi akela hai.

Partial fractions ki shakal
\[\dfrac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)} = \dfrac{A}{1 - x} + \dfrac{Bx + D}{1 + x^2}\]
\[1 + x = A(1 + x^2) + (Bx + D)(1 - x)\]
Kyun: Linear factor \((1 - x)\) ke upar sirf constant \(A\) aata hai. \(1 + x^2\) ke real roots nahi hain (yeh toot nahi sakta), is liye us ke upar linear expression \(Bx + D\) aata hai. Phir dono taraf poore denominator se multiply kiya.

\(A\), \(B\), \(D\) maloom karein
\(x = 1\) rakhein: \(2 = 2A\), to \(A = 1\).
\(x^2\) ke coefficients: \(0 = A - B\), to \(B = 1\).
Constant terms: \(1 = A + D\), to \(D = 0\).
Kyun: \(x = 1\) rakhne se doosri term \((1 - x)\) ki wajah se zero ho jati hai aur \(A\) seedha mil jata hai. Baqi coefficients compare kar ke mile. Tasalli ke liye \(x\) ke coefficient: \(1 = B - D = 1\), theek hai.
Dhyan dein: \((Bx + D)(1 - x)\) ko kholte waqt \(-Bx^2\) ka minus na bhooliye.

Dobara likh kar integrate karein
\[dy = \left(\dfrac{1}{1 - x} + \dfrac{x}{1 + x^2}\right)dx\]
\[y = -\ln|1 - x| + \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1 + x^2) + \ln|C|\]
Kyun: \(1 - x\) ki derivative \(-1\) hai, is liye \(\int\frac{dx}{1 - x} = -\ln|1 - x|\). Doosre hisse mein upar \(x\) hai jo neeche wale \(1 + x^2\) ki derivative \(2x\) ka aadha hai, is liye \(\frac{1}{2}\ln(1 + x^2)\). Constant ko \(\ln|C|\) likha taake logs jur sakein.

Logs jorein
\[y = \ln\left|\dfrac{C\sqrt{1 + x^2}}{1 - x}\right|\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{2}\ln a = \ln\sqrt{a}\); jama wale logs zarb ban jate hain aur minus wala log taqseem. Is tarah teeno terms ek log mein aa gayin, bilkul kitab ke jawab jaisa.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{1 + x^2} + \dfrac{1}{1 - x}\]
\[= \dfrac{x(1 - x) + 1 + x^2}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 + x}{(1 - x)(1 + x^2)}\]
Kyun: Common denominator le kar upar \(x - x^2 + 1 + x^2 = 1 + x\) bacha. Di hui right side mil gayi.
